full_judgment:
120. When the Magistrate has recorded confession in accordance with law, the court shall presume the document is correct and the accused has also signed the confession. In that case a presumption of its correctness can legitimately be drawn in view of the provisions of section 80 of the Evidence Act, 1872. 

 121. Section 80 of the Evidence Act, 1872 provides provisions for general presumption of correctness as to the (a) genuineness of the confession as record of evidence against its maker, (b) the confession was duly taken, and (c) the confession as a document recorded by a learned Magistrate is genuine. Although section 80 of the Evidence Act, 1872 does not make a confession a conclusive proof of guilt against its maker, it carries substantive weight as genuine admission of guilt against its maker unless the presumption is rebutted by the defence by bringing and proving allegations of undue and coercive circumstances. The convict-Appellant in this case hopelessly failed bringing any evidence on record of the court below based on which it can be suggested that true confessions are unreliable and unsafe to base a conviction of death sentence.
